newsitem.title: USA: Clinton healing quickly, plays full round of golf.
newsitem.headline: Clinton healing quickly, plays full round of golf.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Monday played his first full round of golf in four months after doctors praised his extraordinary progress in recovering from a knee injury, the White House said.
Late Monday afternoon, the president went the full 18 holes in blistering heat and unhealthful air conditions at the Army-Navy Country Club outside the nation's capital.
He played alone, and a White House official said it was the first time since returning to the course that he had used his full arsenal of woods and irons.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters earlier that Clinton's doctors carried out an 18-week review of his recovery on Sunday. The president stumbled on a stair after midnight on March 14, tearing a tendon in his right knee.

"They pronounced themselves satisfied that that he has made extraordinarily good progress in his recovery and the president will now be able to move around without the use of his knee brace, except when he plays golf," McCurry said.

The spokesman said Clinton was about a month ahead of schedule in terms of playing golf. At the time of his injury, which required emergency surgery, officials said Clinton was not likely to return to the links until August.
He resumed play June 24, but said Friday that he had played no more than nine holes.
Officials said the president's treatment emphasis has changed.

"The focus now is no longer on protecting the knee muscle itself but on beginning to build the strength up in the knee," McCurry said, adding that Clinton, who turns 51 next month, had begun walking on a treadmill and was expected to begin jogging on it soon.

But he said the doctors had admonished Clinton to be careful when going up and down stairs. Clinton injured his knee when he stumbled on a stair at the Florida estate of professional golfer Greg Norman.
